subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue relying on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This is a new public config and security boundary, and automation should not choose precedence or default message-tool behavior across cron, subagent, sandbox, provider, agent, group, sender, and per-job policy layers without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Define `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the cron-specific hard policy layer, document precedence, and add targeted cron delivery/tool tests.

options.title: Make cron inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as part of the existing subagent restriction model, reducing new config surface but coupling two different runtime concepts.

options.title: Keep per-job controls only
options.body: Decline a system-wide cron policy and document `--tools`/`payload.toolsAllow` as the supported hard-enforcement mechanism for scheduled jobs.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Define `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` as the cron-specific hard policy layer, document precedence, and add targeted cron delivery/tool tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from recent cron/session commits and the prior maintainer-style review on this issue.
